nodes.label: Operator
nodes.description: The local developer exploring the recovered model in es-view. Here they click the 'Data model' tab to see the physical storage the code actually touches (datastores/fields) and which behavioral nodes write/read/project each store.

nodes.label: Web browser (es-view SPA)
nodes.description: The browser running the React explorer SPA. It fetched the whole model once from GET /api/model at boot and holds it in memory; clicking the 'Data model' tab flips the SPA into the DataModel view, which renders the physical layer as a pannable containment graph. The rendering never re-hits the server.

tactical.explanation: Tabs.jsx lists a ['data','Data model'] tab whose onClick calls setMode('data'); App.jsx renders {mode==='data' && <DataModel/>}. DataModel.jsx pulls the already-loaded `model` from the ExplorerProvider context (fetched once via fetchModel -> GET /api/model) and runs the imperative layout into a ref. No network call happens on tab open.

anchors.note: the ['data','Data model'] tab entry
onClick => setMode('data')
mode==='data' mounts <DataModel/>

nodes.label: Connected Claude (MCP client)
nodes.description: A Claude session connected to the es-view MCP server over streamable HTTP. It calls the list_data_model tool to read the SAME recovered data model the operator sees in the Data-model tab, grounding a question like 'what stores does this touch / who writes this store' in the live model the human is exploring.

tactical.explanation: POST /mcp is served in-process by createMcpHandler; buildMcpServer registers list_data_model whose handler returns renderDataModelMarkdown(services). The tool closes over the same shared `services` (model + indexes) the SPA API serves, so operator and Claude read one source of truth. list_data_model does NOT touch the filesystem (unlike the source-grounded tools) — it is a pure in-memory projection.

anchors.note: registerTool 'list_data_model'
handler => renderDataModelMarkdown(services)

nodes.label: Recovered data model
nodes.description: The physical storage the code actually touches, projected from the model as a containment tree of datastores (server/database/table, filesystem/directory/file, broker/queue, in-memory, …) with, for each record set, the behavioral nodes that write/read/project/persist/connect it and each store's demand-driven fields. Shown in the SPA Data-model tab as a pannable graph and returned by the MCP list_data_model tool as a markdown tree — two independent renderers over one projection.

tactical.explanation: TWO renderers, ONE projection over agg-model. SPA: DataModel.jsx filters model.nodes for type datastore/field (dataCount), seeds a collapsed-set via defaultCollapsed (containers with > COLLAPSE_OVER=12 leaf descendants start collapsed), and calls renderDataModelInto — an imperative DOM+SVG layout that builds the datastore forest (isRoot/childStores), grid-packs each container's children ~square (packGrid: cols=ceil(sqrt(n)), shortest-column placement), draws parent->child containment arrows, and per store shows a header count badge + per-verb footer pills from datastoreConsumers (deduped by node+verb), record-set fields via fieldsOf. MCP: renderDataModelMarkdown(services) uses the SHARED selectors dataModelTree(model,nodeById) to build the same forest and lists per record-set consumers as an indented markdown tree. The layout/barycenter/grid math is presentation detail, not domain behavior. Both draw ONLY direct child fields of a record set (one level) and neither renders dataModelTree's looseFields nor nested sub-fields — see hot-data-model-drops-nested-loose-fields. isRecordSet decides card-vs-container. Pure read: no state is written on this path.

anchors.note: dataCount = model.nodes filtered to datastore/field

fields.name: containmentTree
fields.derivation: The datastore containment forest built by following each physical node's `parent` pointer over the model's datastore nodes (server>database>table, filesystem>directory>file, broker>queue, …). A datastore whose parent is missing or is not itself a datastore becomes a root, so nothing is dropped. The SPA grid-packs and draws it with arrows; the MCP renderer indents it as markdown.

sources.note: physical (datastore) nodes read from the loaded model and grouped by parent pointer

evidence.note: SPA isRoot/childStores build the same forest independently

fields.name: storeConsumers
fields.derivation: Per record-set datastore, the behavioral nodes that touch it and the storage verb (writes / persists to / projects from / reads / connects via), gathered from every flow edge whose `to` is that store and deduped by (node,verb). SPA shows a header count badge plus one clickable pill per verb; MCP lists them under each record set.

sources.note: flow edges pointing at each store, resolved to consumer node + verb

evidence.note: edges where e.to === storeId, deduped by node+verb

fields.name: recordSetFields
fields.derivation: For each record set, its DIRECT child `field` nodes (label, dataType, nullable), shown inside the store card / listed under the store in markdown. Demand-driven: only the fields a read model or aggregate actually references appear. One level only — nested sub-fields and orphaned fields are not rendered by either surface.

sources.note: field nodes whose parent === this datastore id

fields.name: collapsedByDefault
fields.derivation: SPA-only presentation state: containers with more than COLLAPSE_OVER (12) leaf-table descendants start collapsed to a single header node (click to expand). The MCP markdown has no collapse and always emits the full tree, so a connected Claude may see more of the tree than the operator's default view.
fields.notes: Computed in the SPA from the datastore forest; not part of the model, not seen by the MCP renderer.

evidence.note: collapse containers with > COLLAPSE_OVER leaf descendants

nodes.label: The Model
nodes.description: The canonical Event Storming model (flows.json): the deduped node set plus flows, hotspots, terms, and derived meta. Built by the merge, then read by the es-view server and the DOT/explorer generator. Its invariants ARE the merge-time validation rules.

tactical.explanation: READ SIDE (this flow): the resolved model is held in memory in `services` (model + indexes + repoRoot) built once by buildServices, and also shipped whole to the SPA via GET /api/model at boot. The Data-model projection reads only its physical sub-layer: model.nodes of type datastore/field plus the flow edges that link behavioral nodes to those stores. The SPA reads its in-memory copy; the MCP tool reads the server's `services.model`. No write occurs on this path.

anchors.note: model + buildIndexes(model) + repoRoot shared by API and MCP
GET /api/model ships the whole model to the SPA once at boot

nodes.label: Local filesystem
nodes.description: The local filesystem outside the process, reached through node:fs. Holds flows.json, the canonical model the es-view server resolves and serves. In this read flow it is only the ultimate origin of the model already loaded into memory; the Data-model projection never touches disk.

tactical.explanation: The server resolves flows.json from disk at boot (resolve-model.mjs) into `services.model`; from then on both the SPA (via /api/model) and the MCP list_data_model read that in-memory model, so this flow's rendering does no filesystem IO.

anchors.note: the resolved model that originated from the filesystem

nodes.label: flows.json (canonical model)
nodes.description: The canonical model file. Its node set includes the very datastore/field nodes this Data-model projection renders, so rm-data-model projects the physical layer out of the file whose whole graph it is a view of (a self-referential loop in the self-model).

tactical.explanation: Resolved once at server boot into services.model and served to the SPA via GET /api/model; the Data-model tab and list_data_model both project the datastore/field nodes and their edges out of that loaded copy.

anchors.note: GET /api/model returns resolved.model (from flows.json)

flows.name: Operator opens the Data-model tab (and Claude reads the same via list_data_model)
flows.summary: The operator clicks the 'Data model' tab in the es-view SPA. Without any server round-trip, the DataModel view filters the already-loaded model for its physical layer (datastore/field nodes) and renders a pannable containment graph: nested store cards with parent->child arrows, a per-store badge counting the behavioral nodes that touch it, per-verb footer pills, and each record set's demand-driven fields; big containers start collapsed. A connected Claude session reads the SAME recovered data model over MCP by calling list_data_model, which renders it as an indented markdown tree. Both surfaces are pure reads projecting one source of truth (agg-model) through two independent renderers, so a human's exploration and a model's grounding stay in lockstep.
flows.trigger: Operator clicks the 'Data model' tab (Tabs.jsx setMode('data')); or a connected Claude calls the MCP tool list_data_model.

hotspots.label: Data-model tab counts fields it never renders (nested sub-fields and loose fields)
hotspots.description: DataModel.jsx's header count (`dataCount`) counts EVERY datastore + field node in the model, but both renderers draw only the DIRECT `field` children of a rendered record set: the SPA's fieldsOf(id) and the MCP markdown's per-store fields line each go exactly one level deep. Nested sub-fields (a field whose parent is another field) and loose fields (a field parented to nothing or to a non-datastore) are counted but never shown on the canvas or in the markdown — even though selectors.mjs already provides fieldTree() for nested fields and dataModelTree()'s looseFields for orphans, which neither renderer wires up. Human question: is the one-level-of-fields rendering intentional (keep the graph shallow), or should the Data-model tab render nested/loose fields so the 'Data model N' badge matches what is actually drawn?

tactical.explanation: DataModel.jsx:16 dataCount = model.nodes.filter(datastore|field).length feeds the header badge and the empty-state gate. datamodel-layout.js:50 fieldsOf(id) = fields with parent===id (direct only); buildCard iterates fieldsOf(ds.id) with no recursion into sub-fields. context.mjs renderDataModelMarkdown lists dataModelTree's per-node `fields` (childFields, one level) and walks only `roots`+`stores`, never emitting looseFields. selectors.mjs:104 fieldTree() (nested) and :88 looseFields (orphans) exist but are unused by both the tab and the tool, so any nested/loose field inflates the count without appearing.

anchors.note: dataCount counts ALL datastore+field nodes
fieldsOf: direct field children only, no sub-field recursion
looseFields computed but rendered by neither surface
nested-field support that the renderers do not use
markdown per-store fields also one level; looseFields never emitted
